title: Ralph's clarinet and fingering shortcuts
summary: Ralph's clarinet and Manetta's lessons lead Hall to demonstrate short cuts for C sharp and B flat and fork fingerings.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: That I got from Miller Barnes. I know Barnes. He, it's not his regular one but he had this one, saw that it was fair and he said he didn't think he was going to play anymore and did I know anybody who wanted to buy it so I said well I'd like to buy it. That's what started the whole thing. Can you play anything in that one? No, just a few little exercises or so. I can play a little bit of tunes when they're written but I can't… Can't fake anything? No.

Well he's made up a couple of little tunes. Like one day he said he was practicing and came across the first two or three notes of the world is waiting for the sunrise and he's able to go ahead and play the rest of it. So he'll make it all right I think if he can get his fingers to work.

Manetta is teaching me right now to concentrate on like when your fingers are working up here and then you have to go all the way down. All the way down yeah. And I have trouble. I have trouble getting from up here to down there. Like from B flat to B natural. Yeah.

Well that's what matters Bob. You practice. I know they say you just do no breakers. Yeah. You keep carrying right out. I tell you what. Like different she's making now. A B flat and a B natural. But the only thing that this kind of… Hold this down. That hand down. The right hand down. Half of your work is right there. Yeah. Having the right hand down all the time. And it's a lot of short cuts to a lot of those. See now I did this line.

And if you want to make C sharp instead of figuring your C sharp like that. In a fast. If you're going to hold that note. This is the C sharp you'd hold. But now if you're going to make a fast passage you hit this key. Oh. That's fantastic.

You see that much. That's this is much easier than to do this one. Oh yeah. Sure. That's what you call your short cut. Oh. and left little finger there on the... If you want to make B-flat, you can fork B-flat like that. Alright, that's in a fast passage. But if you want to hold it, and you're playing with other instruments, you make it this way, that's the best way, because that's the real way to make it. That's with the two fingers, then you're...
